title: Establish compact swapflow and layer signatures for control atoms
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our Figma library contains multiple ‘control atoms’ (buttons, toggles, small charts/table headers) that have diverging variant shapes, inconsistent layer naming, and fragile auto-layout rules. This causes frequent regressions when teams override instances, and our CI publish process sometimes rejects libraries due to duplicated variant IDs or ambiguous layer signatures.

Goal: Consolidate compact control atoms into a deterministic swapflow (stable instance replacement path) + enforce a layer signature convention so instance overrides and programmatic exports remain stable. Deliver a safe publish pipeline with preflight checks and a short remediation playbook for engineers consuming the library.
acceptance_criteria: All compact control atoms (button-small, icon-button, dense-toggle, compact-row-header) follow the new layer signature pattern: <role> / <element> / <state> / [token-ref].
Auto-layout rules for compact controls are normalized: horizontal axis, spacing tokens from tokens/compact-spacing, and a single pinned child for icon alignment.
Swapflow documented: steps to replace legacy instances without breaking overrides; Figma plugin quick-script (or copy-paste checklist) validated.
Publish preflight (Figma + CI) flags duplicate variant names, missing token refs, and invalid constraint configurations; zero blocking errors for the updated library.
Design and Engineering sign-off obtained. QA spot-checks on 8 consumer files (dashboard, chat, embed, analytics page) show no visual regressions beyond documented acceptable deltas.

Define auto-layout canonical rules and map to tokens/compact-spacing (design + eng)
Create swapflow migration checklist and small Figma script for instance swap (engineering)
Run preflight checks in staging publish pipeline and update warnings/errors (platform eng)
Pilot bulk-replace in 3 consumer files and record any override breakages (design QA)
Finalize docs, update component README, and merge to library publish branch
decisions: Adopt terse hierarchical layer signatures instead of long descriptive layers to reduce token noise (agreed 2026-02-25).
Prefer composition over boolean variant explosion: combine 'compact' state as a separate boolean variant rather than separate full variant sets for each density.
Publishing CI will block on duplicate variant IDs and missing token references; non-critical spacing deltas surface as warnings only for one release.
Do not perform bulk rename across full library in a single PR; use staged rollout per consumer to minimize override breakage.
